Validate exported outputs before saving

Source: R/validate_export_outputs.R
validate_export_outputs.Rd

Checks every output that the export/Save flow would write, so a save can be refused before any file is created. It combines two levels of checking:

Usage

validate_export_outputs(
  output,
  obj_names = NULL,
  metadata = metadata_nca_variables,
  grouping_vars = character(0)
)

Arguments

output

The export list as assembled for the Save flow: a named, possibly nested list of outputs (plots, tables, and *_code strings), with the CDISC datasets under a CDISC element keyed pp/adpp/adnca.

obj_names

Optional character vector of leaf names that will be written. When NULL (the default) every leaf is validated.

metadata

Metadata data frame passed to validate_cdisc_types() for the CDISC value-level checks. Defaults to metadata_nca_variables.

grouping_vars

Selected custom grouping variables allowed in ADPP/ADNCA, passed to validate_cdisc_types(). Known fields and PP remain strictly checked.

Value

A tidy findings data frame with columns Output, Variable, Check, Severity, Expected, Observed, and Message. Variable is NA for object-class findings and holds the column name for CDISC value-level findings. Zero rows means every output is safe to export.

Details

  • Object class for all outputs: plot nodes must be a ggplot or plotly, table nodes must be a data frame, and *_code nodes must be a length-1 character string. Anything the export writer cannot serialise is reported as an error.

  • Value level for the CDISC datasets: the pp/adpp/adnca entries under CDISC are additionally checked against the metadata-declared data types and lengths via validate_cdisc_types().

The walk mirrors the export writer: plain lists are recursed into, and when obj_names is supplied only those named leaves (the ones that will actually be written) are validated.

Examples

output <- list(
  nca_results = list(nca_pkparam = data.frame(AVAL = 1.2)),
  CDISC = list(adnca = data.frame(STUDYID = "S1", AVAL = 1.2))
)
validate_export_outputs(output)
#> [1] Output   Variable Check    Severity Expected Observed Message 
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
